text:
name: lampOS on ARM64

# Builds and tests lampOS natively on Linux ARM64 for every pull request into
# lamp-voice and every push to lamp-voice, on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), so the binaries also run on the
# lamps' Debian 12 (glibc 2.36). Not in a container: tests that take a
# permission away must not run as root. The binaries are kept
# as an artifact for a week, with their SHA-256, so the first builder can put
# a builder's work on a lamp without building it again. See
# lampOS/docs/joining.md.
#
# The tests are split across four runners (cargo-nextest partitions), each
# still running one test at a time, as on a lamp's few cores: one serial run
# took about 20 of the job's 30 minutes. Doc tests, the two tests with their
# own harness and the binaries' artifact come from the first runner only.
#
# The realtime group (tests that wait on the real clock, 977 s of the 1,191 s
# of test time on 2026-10-15; nextest group `realtime` in
# lampOS/.config/nextest.toml) runs only in the full run: every night, started
# from main by .github/workflows/lampos-nightly.yml as a manual run of this
# workflow on lamp-voice with `full`. A failed full run opens an issue. See
# lampOS/docs/realtime-tests.md.
#
#            | runners | profile   | tests at once | realtime | crates tested
# pull req.  | 1       | `pr`      | one per core  | skipped  | its own, their users, three readers (below)
# lamp-voice | 1       | `pr`      | one per core  | skipped  | all (binaries for updates.md)
# full       | 4       | `default` | one           | run      | all
#
# A pull request tests only the crates its diff changes, every crate that
# depends on them, and lamp-cloud, lamp-voice-eval and lamp-update, whose
# tests read other crates' files (the project lead's proposal, 19 Oct 2026,
# #1711; .github/scripts/lampos-pr-crates.py). Cargo.lock, any Cargo.toml,
# crates/msgs, bus and ipc, deploy/, skills/, the docs tests read, .config/,
# the script, this workflow and any other path run every crate. The run's
# summary says what was tested and why.
#
# Every binary and every test binary is still built for the whole workspace,
# so dependencies are built with one set of features and come from the cache;
# a pull request picks its crates' tests with a nextest filter (`package(...)`),
# not `-p`, which resolved other features and rebuilt 73 dependencies in
# 39531799004. Only what changed is built again:
# .github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py gives each source file whose content
# the cached build had its time back, so cargo rebuilds only changed crates and
# the crates built from them, not all of lampOS on every checkout (#1806; the
# first builder's ask of 21 Oct 2026 for runs of about ten minutes, against 11
# to 28 and 19 at the median: 3.9 to 4.4 minutes in the probe runs there).
# Publication-eligible pushes are the exception: they restore neither target
# nor source times, and record fresh checkout times in an empty target before
# building. Their signed binaries do not depend on cache freshness. PRs and
# publication-disabled runs keep the ordinary cached path below.
#
# The cache is lamp-voice's newest build: each of lamp-voice's own runs saves
# it under a key with its commit, even when a test failed, and pull requests
# restore it and don't save. No lamp-voice run is cancelled while it waits
# (the concurrency below), so each commit's build is saved. A key on
# Cargo.lock alone was saved once and never renewed, and each pull request's own 1 GB cache, which
# no other run could use, pushed the repository past GitHub's 10 GB, so
# lamp-voice's was thrown out and 6 of 30 pull requests built cold (#1806; the
# lead, 21 Oct 2026). Until #1712 lands, a pull request onto its branch saves
# when it found nothing to restore, as before: nothing else saves a cache it
# may read (its own, its base's or main's; the reviewer on #2454).
#
# Without the realtime group the tests take about 4 minutes of test time,
# mostly quick unit tests, so one runner runs them as many at once as it has
# cores. Each runner compiles every test binary again (about 5 of its 10
# minutes on 2026-10-15), so more runners would only cost more. The full run
# keeps four, one test at a time, for the realtime tests.

# Not on every push to every builder's branch: with nine builders and four
# runners a run, that queued eleven runs behind eight on 2026-10-15, lamp-voice's
# own among them. A builder's work is run when its pull request is opened or
# pushed to, or by hand (Actions, "Run workflow", on its branch).
on:
  push:
    branches: ['lamp-voice']
    paths: ['lampOS/**', '.github/workflows/lampos-arm64.yml', '.github/scripts/lampos-pr-crates.py', '.github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py', '.github/scripts/lampos-publish*.py']
  # A pull request that changes only docs a build never reads skips this run (the
  # project lead, 19 Oct 2026, #1711): the docs' and the role files' Markdown. The
  # docs that code or tests read are named again below, so a change to one still
  # runs. lampOS/crates/update/tests/it/ci_paths.rs fails when a crate reads one that
  # isn't (#1791's guard). A
  # skill's SKILL.md is part of the skill, so lampOS/skills/** always runs. The
  # push to lamp-voice keeps every run: its artifact is what lamps install.
  # Such a PR merges without ARM64 once the reviewer has read it
  # (builders/reviewer.md).
  # #1712's branch too while the second route is built on it: a pull request
  # onto it gets its run on open and on each push (19 Oct 21:1x). Back to
  # lamp-voice alone once #1712 lands.
  pull_request:
    branches: ['lamp-voice', 'first/voice-cascade-gemini']
    paths:
      - 'lampOS/**'
      - '!lampOS/docs/**/*.md'
      - '!lampOS/builders/**'
      - 'lampOS/docs/attention.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/brain-build.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/endpoint-detection.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/endpoint-pilot.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/install.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/memory.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/switches.md'
      - '.github/workflows/lampos-arm64.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/lampos-pr-crates.py'
      - '.github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py'
      - '.github/scripts/lampos-publish*.py'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      full:
        description: 'Full run: every test including the realtime group, four runners, one test at a time (the nightly run)'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A full run has its own group, so a merge never cancels the nightly run.
  # Each of lamp-voice's runs has a group of its own commit, so none is
  # cancelled: a group keeps one run waiting, and a newer merge replaced it.
  # On 21 Oct 7 of 15 lamp-voice runs were cancelled that way, each one a
  # commit with no binaries for the lamps and the cache not renewed
  # (devops007-P2 on #1806). Runs of commits close together now run side by
  # side, one runner each.
  group: lampos-arm64-${{ inputs.full && 'full-' || '' }}${{ github.event.pull_request.number || (github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice' && github.sha) || github.ref }}
  # A newer push to a pull request makes the running one moot: it is cancelled.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/lamp-voice' }}

jobs:
  arm64:
    name: lampOS — build and test on Linux ARM64 (${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 90
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Four for a full run (every test, one at a time), otherwise one.
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.full && '[1, 2, 3, 4]' || '[1]') }}
    steps:
      - name: system packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            ca-certificates curl git build-essential pkg-config clang libclang-dev libasound2-dev procps file
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # A pull request's merge commit and its first parent (lamp-voice), for the crates it changes.
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: publication failure tests (offline, no signing secret)
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-publish-test.py
      - name: Rust 1.96.0
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal --default-toolchain 1.96.0 -c clippy -c rustfmt
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: artifact provenance regression (offline, disposable Cargo workspace)
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: python3 -B -I .github/scripts/lampos-publish-artifact-test.py
      - name: restore the cache
        id: cache
        # Match publish's eligibility exactly, so signing candidates build cold.
        if: >-
          ${{ !(github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          && github.repository == 'autonomous-ai/lampOS' && vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH == 'on') }}
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            lampOS/target
          key: lampos-arm64-u2204-${{ hashFiles('lampOS/Cargo.lock') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            lampos-arm64-u2204-${{ hashFiles('lampOS/Cargo.lock') }}-
            lampos-arm64-u2204-
      - name: unchanged source files get the cached build's times back
        if: >-
          ${{ !(github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          && github.repository == 'autonomous-ai/lampOS' && vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH == 'on') }}
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py
      - name: record fresh source times for a cold publication build
        if: >-
          github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          && github.repository == 'autonomous-ai/lampOS' && vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH == 'on'
        # With no target/record, this only records checkout times for the cache
        # saved after the run. Any unexpected pre-existing target fails closed.
        run: |
          if [ -e lampOS/target ] || [ -L lampOS/target ]; then
            echo 'cold publication build requires an absent lampOS/target' >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest
      - name: build (release, the lamps' binaries)
        working-directory: lampOS
        # Keep Cargo's current-target records outside the restored target cache.
        run: cargo build --locked --release --workspace --bins --examples --message-format=json-render-diagnostics > arm64-build.jsonl
      - name: every built lamp-* binary is classified for the lamp-os package
        working-directory: lampOS
        run: bash tools/package-binaries-test.sh && bash tools/package-binaries.sh deploy/package-binaries.json target/release
      - name: build the two selected artifact examples without filename collisions
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        working-directory: lampOS
        # Both controls and expression have replay_cost. Export expression's
        # planner tool from a separate target directory; the workspace gate
        # above still builds every example from both packages.
        run: |
          cargo build --locked --release -p lamp-schedule --example schedule_check \
            --target-dir target/lampos-artifact-examples --message-format=json-render-diagnostics > arm64-schedule-example.jsonl
          cargo build --locked --release -p lamp-expression --example replay_cost \
            --target-dir target/lampos-artifact-examples --message-format=json-render-diagnostics > arm64-expression-example.jsonl
      - name: publication CLI rehearsal (local test key and simulated GitHub only)
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-publish-cli-test.py --updater lampOS/target/release/lamp-update
      - name: which crates a pull request tests
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-pr-crates.py
      - name: test (full run, every test one at a time; otherwise without the realtime group, in parallel)
        working-directory: lampOS
        # The two tests with their own harness (harness = false) cannot be listed by nextest; the first runner runs them below.
        # Profile `pr` skips the realtime group (lampOS/.config/nextest.toml); the -E below is intersected with it.
        # A full run uses `default`: every test, one at a time. A pull request's picked crates narrow the -E.
        env:
          PICKED: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.filter }}
        run: |
          echo "cores: $(nproc)"
          filter='not (binary_id(lamp-ipc::relay_signals) | binary_id(lamp-turn-end-wire::process))'
          if [ -n "$PICKED" ]; then filter="$filter & ($PICKED)"; fi
          cargo nextest run --locked --release --workspace \
            --profile ${{ inputs.full && 'default' || 'pr' }} \
            --no-tests=pass -j ${{ inputs.full && '1' || 'num-cpus' }} \
            --partition hash:${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }} \
            -E "$filter"
      - name: doc tests and the own-harness tests (nextest runs neither)
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        working-directory: lampOS
        run: |
          cargo test --locked --release --workspace --doc -- --test-threads=1
          cargo test --locked --release -p lamp-ipc --test relay_signals
          cargo test --locked --release -p lamp-turn-end-wire --test process
      - name: export only current Cargo targets and their SHA-256
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: >-
          python3 -B -I .github/scripts/lampos-publish-artifact.py --workspace lampOS
          --build-log lampOS/arm64-build.jsonl
          --build-log lampOS/arm64-schedule-example.jsonl
          --build-log lampOS/arm64-expression-example.jsonl
          --out lampOS/arm64-out
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        with:
          # A pull request runs on its merge with lamp-voice; the name is its own head commit.
          name: lampos-arm64-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          path: lampOS/arm64-out/
          retention-days: 7
      # lamp-voice's own, and one onto #1712's that found none (see the top). Not
      # a run by hand on another branch: no pull request reads its cache (the
      # reviewer on #2465).
      - name: discard the isolated example target before saving the cache
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.shard == 1 && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          || (github.base_ref == 'first/voice-cascade-gemini' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-matched-key == '')) }}
        # The CI artifact has independent, checksummed copies of both examples.
        run: rm -rf -- lampOS/target/lampos-artifact-examples
      - name: save the cache
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.shard == 1 && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          || (github.base_ref == 'first/voice-cascade-gemini' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-matched-key == '')) }}
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            lampOS/target
          # A cold publication build skipped restore, so it has no cache outputs.
          key: ${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-primary-key || format('lampos-arm64-u2204-{0}-{1}', hashFiles('lampOS/Cargo.lock'), github.sha) }}

  publish:
    name: lampOS — sign and publish the tested lamp-voice artifact
    needs: arm64
    # Off until the owner explicitly activates publication. Manual runs and PRs
    # never enter this job; download-artifact defaults to this successful run.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice' && github.repository == 'autonomous-ai/lampOS' && vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH == 'on'
    # The owner must configure branch-only lamp-voice protection before storing
    # the signing key here; naming an environment does not create its rules.
    environment: lampos-update-publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
    concurrency:
      group: lampos-publish-lamp-voice
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lampos-arm64-${{ github.sha }}
          path: build
      - name: verify, sign, upload, then promote the channel
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH: ${{ vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_PUBLISH }}
          LAMPOS_UPDATE_BOOTSTRAP: ${{ vars.LAMPOS_UPDATE_BOOTSTRAP }}
          # Use the branch-restricted environment secret, with no repository or
          # organization copy. Only this step references it in this workflow.
          # Cleanup removes its 0600 file on normal failure;
          # forced runner termination still relies on ephemeral-runner disposal.
          LAMPOS_UPDATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.LAMPOS_UPDATE_KEY }}
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-publish.py --artifact build --source .

  # A full run that fails opens an issue (or comments on the open one), so a
  # realtime test broken by a merge is not left unseen: no other run has it.
  report-full-run-failure:
    needs: arm64
    if: failure() && inputs.full
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      TITLE: 'lampOS: the full ARM64 run failed'
      BODY: >-
        The full ARM64 run (realtime tests included) failed on ${{ github.ref_name }} at
        ${{ github.sha }}: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}.
        Pull requests and merges skip the realtime group (lampOS/docs/realtime-tests.md),
        so the change that broke it may have passed its own run.
    steps:
      - run: |
          n=$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$TITLE\" in:title" --json number -q '.[0].number')
          if [ -n "$n" ]; then gh issue comment "$n" --body "$BODY"; else gh issue create --title "$TITLE" --body "$BODY"; fi

name: lampOS clippy

# Clippy over the whole lampOS workspace, every target, warnings as errors, on
# x86 Linux, for every pull request into lamp-voice (and #1712's branch) and
# every push to lamp-voice (the first builder, #1722, 20 Oct 2026 05:35). It is
# the builders' gate (lampOS/docs/joining.md) for every crate at once. On 19
# and 20 Oct two breaks passed unseen: a dead copy on lamp-voice (#2008), and
# #1944's break of lamp-voice's tests on #1712, which ARM64 caught only on the
# next pull request, because a pull request's ARM64 run builds and tests only
# the crates it changes and their users (lampos-arm64.yml).
#
# A workflow of its own: ci.yml skips every lampOS change, and a step in the
# ARM64 run would add to that run's time. Linux, so the cfg(target_os = "linux")
# code a Mac's gate skips is checked too. Its triggers are the ARM64 run's.
#
# Its cache is restored as the ARM64 run's is (lampos-arm64.yml, #1806), and
# each unchanged source file is given back the time the cached build had for
# it, so clippy checks only what changed since that build. It is saved under a
# key on Cargo.lock alone, by lamp-voice's first run after the lockfile
# changes, and by no run that found that key: a save under each commit's key
# (about 2.2 GB) filled 13.3 of the repository's 14.7 GB on 21 Oct and pushed
# the ARM64 run's caches out of GitHub's 10 GB (devops007 on #1806). Pull
# requests restore it and don't save, but for one onto #1712's branch that
# found none.
on:
  push:
    branches: ['lamp-voice']
    paths: ['lampOS/**', '.github/workflows/lampos-clippy.yml', '.github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py']
  pull_request:
    branches: ['lamp-voice', 'first/voice-cascade-gemini']
    paths:
      - 'lampOS/**'
      - '!lampOS/docs/**/*.md'
      - '!lampOS/builders/**'
      - 'lampOS/docs/attention.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/brain-build.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/endpoint-detection.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/endpoint-pilot.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/install.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/memory.md'
      - 'lampOS/docs/switches.md'
      - '.github/workflows/lampos-clippy.yml'
      - '.github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: lampos-clippy-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  # A newer push to a pull request makes the running one moot.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/lamp-voice' }}

jobs:
  clippy:
    name: lampOS — clippy, every crate and target (x86 Linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: system packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            ca-certificates curl git build-essential pkg-config clang libclang-dev libasound2-dev
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Rust 1.96.0
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal --default-toolchain 1.96.0 -c clippy
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: restore the cache
        id: cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            lampOS/target
          key: lampos-clippy-u2204-${{ hashFiles('lampOS/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            lampos-clippy-u2204-
      - name: unchanged source files get the cached build's times back
        run: python3 -I .github/scripts/lampos-source-times.py
      - name: clippy (every crate and target, warnings as errors)
        working-directory: lampOS
        run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: save the cache
        if: >-
          ${{ !cancelled() && steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/lamp-voice'
          || (github.base_ref == 'first/voice-cascade-gemini' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-matched-key == '')) }}
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            lampOS/target
          key: ${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

# cargo-nextest configuration for the lampOS workspace.
#
# The realtime group: tests that wait on the real clock for seconds by design
# (the production capture loop played in real time, a program's real report
# period against the bus's real lease, a real grace before a kill). On
# 2026-10-15 the group had 123 tests, 977 s of the 1,191 s spent on all 4,507
# tests, so pull requests skipped it. Most have since moved onto test clocks
# (#823). The 8 left took 35.4 s one after another on ARM64 on 2026-10-17,
# and held their bounds beside a full core load in five runs (#1292), so
# every run now runs them: one at a time (the group) and started first (its
# priority), beside the rest. Run them alone with profile `realtime`. See
# docs/realtime-tests.md. Two of `lamp-skills`' tests joined on 2026-10-19:
# they run the real program on the host's clock by design (#1806). A third
# the same day waits for the real program to start under load (#1829),
# and two more start it twice on the host's clock, a restart between
# (#1837). Two of `lamp-voice`'s hand-controls tests joined the same day
# too: they count the input pump's real wakes for a second by design (#1806).
#
# The same filterset appears twice below (the group override and
# `realtime`'s selection). Keep both identical.

# The group's `priority` needs nextest 0.9.91 or later; an older one stops
# here and says so, rather than ignoring the key (Nine on #1299).
nextest-version = { required = "0.9.91" }

[test-groups]
# One at a time: these tests measure real time and must not compete.
realtime = { max-threads = 1 }

[[profile.default.overrides]]
filter = '''
    (binary_id(lamp-voice::it) & test(/^capture_hold_worker::/))
  | (binary_id(lamp-voice) & test(=coordinator::tests::endpoint_session::endpoint_fixture_reaps_on_panic_before_and_after_handoff))
  | (binary_id(lamp-health::it) & test(=program::between_two_healths_five_seconds_apart_the_program_is_not_taken_for_gone))
  | (binary_id(lamp-skills::it) & (test(=skills::asking_the_policy_on_the_hosts_clock_gives_up_after_its_wait) | test(=skills::a_reading_pose_is_held_on_the_mood_socket_for_its_for_and_then_let_go) | test(=skills::asking_the_policy_a_hello_made_and_not_noticed_rests) | test(=skills::the_program_keeps_a_skill_off_across_a_restart) | test(=skills::the_program_forgets_a_snooze_at_a_restart)))
  | (binary_id(lamp-voice) & (test(=hand_controls::tests::with_the_wait_an_idle_pump_wakes_five_times_a_second_and_stops_at_once) | test(=hand_controls::tests::with_the_wait_an_owner_polling_every_2_ms_does_not_wake_the_pump)))
'''
test-group = 'realtime'
# Started first, so that its one-at-a-time chain runs beside the rest rather
# than after it.
priority = 100
# A passing test's output at the end of every run: `capture_hold_worker`
# prints the medians it bounds, so a drift toward a bound shows before it
# turns a run red (the reviewer on #1299).
success-output = "final"

# speaker_lapse_worker's two tests start a speaker worker, which ends when a
# control message reaches it more than 100 ms after it was sent (the
# channel's bound). On ARM64, beside the rest of a pull request's tests, its
# third message was read 126 to 138 ms late, three times, both tests
# together (#1569 row 42). With every core to themselves, nothing else runs
# while they start. They take about 0.6 s each.
[[profile.default.overrides]]
filter = 'binary_id(lamp-voice::it) & test(/^speaker_lapse_worker::/)'
threads-required = "num-cpus"

# `privacy_worker` says when it begins a test again because its own Controls
# producer was held up (#1569 row 45), so how often that happens shows in
# every run's output, passing ones included (the reviewer on #2234).
[[profile.default.overrides]]
filter = 'binary_id(lamp-voice::it) & test(/^privacy_worker::/)'
success-output = "final"

# Pull requests and pushes to lamp-voice on GitHub Actions
# (.github/workflows/lampos-arm64.yml): every test, the realtime group
# included. A filter given on the command line is intersected with this.
[profile.pr]
default-filter = 'all()'

# By hand: only the realtime group, e.g.
#   cargo nextest run --release --workspace --profile realtime -j 1
[profile.realtime]
default-filter = '''
    (binary_id(lamp-voice::it) & test(/^capture_hold_worker::/))
  | (binary_id(lamp-voice) & test(=coordinator::tests::endpoint_session::endpoint_fixture_reaps_on_panic_before_and_after_handoff))
  | (binary_id(lamp-health::it) & test(=program::between_two_healths_five_seconds_apart_the_program_is_not_taken_for_gone))
  | (binary_id(lamp-skills::it) & (test(=skills::asking_the_policy_on_the_hosts_clock_gives_up_after_its_wait) | test(=skills::a_reading_pose_is_held_on_the_mood_socket_for_its_for_and_then_let_go) | test(=skills::asking_the_policy_a_hello_made_and_not_noticed_rests) | test(=skills::the_program_keeps_a_skill_off_across_a_restart) | test(=skills::the_program_forgets_a_snooze_at_a_restart)))
  | (binary_id(lamp-voice) & (test(=hand_controls::tests::with_the_wait_an_idle_pump_wakes_five_times_a_second_and_stops_at_once) | test(=hand_controls::tests::with_the_wait_an_owner_polling_every_2_ms_does_not_wake_the_pump)))
'''
